page: Amazon Web Services im4gn.8xlarge is a storage-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and custom AWS Graviton2 processors built on the 64-bit Arm Neoverse-N1 architecture. The instance provides 32 dedicated physical cores running at 2.5 GHz with a single thread per core, accompanied by 128 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Internal cache includes 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache pool. Hardware-accelerated cryptographic processing is enabled via dedicated AES instructions, while x86-specific vector instruction sets are absent. Baseline network throughput reaches up to 50 Gbps.

Local high-speed persistence is anchored by 15,000 GB of directly attached NVMe SSD storage. Benchmark telemetry reflects steady I/O and parallel throughput capabilities, registering 20,399.25 operations in Passmark database tests and 38.19 million operations per second during Redis SET workloads. Memory subsystem bandwidth maintains 162.83 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads and 72.97 GB/sec on writes. Static web serving throughput settles at 33.22 GB/sec. These results indicate balanced throughput across parallel I/O and memory transfers.

Compute benchmarks show divergence between single-threaded and scale-out performance. The Geekbench single-core score of 941.0 and single-threaded gzip compression at 20.29 GB/sec represent lower tier throughput, constrained by modest base clock speeds. Conversely, parallel execution scales reliably, evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 11,490.0, Clang software compilation at 24,830.0, and a multi-core stress-ng rating of 48,576.94. The architecture delivers cost efficiency by pairing high local NVMe storage density and power-efficient Arm cores, avoiding the overhead of external network-attached volumes for I/O-intensive datasets.

Given its combination of 15 TB local NVMe storage, 50 Gbps network bandwidth, and 32 dedicated Arm cores, Amazon Web Services im4gn.8xlarge is suited for distributed data stores, NoSQL databases, search indexing engines, log analytics platforms, and real-time data streaming pipelines. Tasks reliant on single-thread execution speed or specialized x86 vector extensions represent architectural bottlenecks.
description: Amazon Web Services im4gn.8xlarge is a storage-optimized virtual machine featuring 32 dedicated 64-bit Arm Neoverse-N1 cores operating at 2.5 GHz and 128 GB of system memory. Built on the AWS Nitro System, the instance incorporates 15,000 GB of integrated NVMe SSD local storage alongside 50 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. Synthetic benchmarks show robust parallel performance, yielding 38.19 million Redis SET operations per second and a multi-core stress-ng result of 48,576.94, contrasted by modest single-threaded performance seen in a 941.0 Geekbench single-core score. Cost efficiency is achieved through the integration of massive local solid-state storage and power-efficient Arm compute cores. This platform is well aligned with high-throughput transactional databases, distributed NoSQL systems, search clusters, and real-time log ingestion workloads.
